intent: Create one 9:16 vertical editorial botanical print composition: two fern fronds printed directly on book cloth and a smaller related paper study.

content_scope.basis: The brief asks for fern structures and a related printed study on cloth.

decisions.subject_basis: Two authored fern fronds with continuous central stems and paired leaflets; recognize each as a flat printed botanical image.

scene.carrier: Opaque fine book cloth carrying two spot-printed fern fronds and one bounded paper study.
scene.intent: Compare the same botanical structure through two print surfaces.
scene.support: Cloth lies flat on a studio board; the complete paper rests on that surface.

candidates.cue: The fronds offer repeated leaflets and two unequal central axes.
candidates.basis: The authored fern structures provide both the carrier graphic and the paper study.
candidates.proposal: Make the two fronds the main carrier print and use a small paper image to compare a single leaflet group.
candidates.contribution: Connect the subject through visible repeated structures and clearly different printing surfaces.
candidates.scene_fit: The fronds share the carrier plane; the small rectangular paper adds one readable physical layer.

decisions.selection_reason: The two larger printed fronds establish the subject; the smaller paper image explains its structure.

design.idea: Two related forms across woven ink and fine printed paper.

pairings.relation: The two fern fronds on cloth share their leaflet pattern with the small paper study.
pairings.purpose: Create a main subject and a legible supporting comparison.

design.composition: Complete 9:16 vertical composition, viewed perpendicularly from above. Two unequal fern fronds cross gently in the upper two thirds; a complete smaller rectangular paper study sits below to the right. Preserve continuous cloth margins and readable boundaries.
design.materials: Fine opaque book cloth with restrained crossed fibers; substantial warm cream and deep olive spot inks follow the same carrier relief. A thin uncoated rectangular paper sheet carries a small botanical reproduction and has its own paper edge and soft contact shadow.
design.palette: Muted green cloth supports cream and deep olive carrier inks; a neutral ivory paper study uses restrained source-consistent green reproduction.

art_direction.selection_basis: Quiet botanical comparison on a woven field.

carrier.color_basis: Authored muted green supports the warm cream fronds and lets the smaller ivory paper read second.

zones.treatment: Two authored fern silhouettes with continuous central stems and paired leaflets are flat warm cream and deep olive deposited ink on the woven carrier.

style_selection.selection_basis: Use the selected process to express this surface and preserve the authored leaf structure.

zones.treatment: A bounded small uncoated-paper image repeats the fern leaflet structure with a restrained green palette and fine tone-dependent screen.

style_selection.selection_basis: Use the selected process to express this surface and preserve the authored leaf structure.

review_targets: Requested 9:16 format and all required frond and paper boundaries remain readable.
Two fern fronds read as carrier ink with recognizable paired leaflets and continuous stems.
The ink follows the same fiber relief as the cloth while broad fills remain substantially opaque.
The paper image, edges and contact share one plane; paper tooth and woven carrier have distinct structures.
Fine print evidence supports a clear whole-frame hierarchy at normal size.
